components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.375rem; max-width: 18rem; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-input { height: 2.5rem; padding: 0 0.75rem; border-radius: 0.75rem; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-control); background: var(--color-surface); color: var(--color-ink); font-size: 0.875rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: var(--color-border-strong); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-brand); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-brand); } .ds-field-hint { font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--color-ink-subtle); }

narrative.overview:
Kerf should feel like walking into a clean, well-organised shop. The floor is swept and the bins are labelled. Every tool hangs where you expect it, and the one thing that needs your attention is marked in amber. The surfaces are warm and calm: cream board, white sheets, ink in a warm near-black. The colour comes from the saw cut in the logo, and it's spent only on the action that moves a job forward.

This is an Operate system first. Owners, estimators, storekeepers, accountants and operators each spend their day in it, on a desk monitor, on a phone in the field, or on a shared tablet by a machine. The quality shows as precision: figures line up in their columns, states are unmistakable, and controls are big enough to hit with a thumb. Expression lives in a few precise details. The sidebar's tiles are amber only on the action that counts, near-black marks where you are, and the corners are soft and friendly.

We reject two looks outright. One is the generic SaaS dashboard: purple gradients, glassy cards, decorative charts with no numbers. The other is the playful consumer app: big illustrations, emoji everywhere, bouncy motion.
keyCharacteristics: A warm cream canvas with opaque white working surfaces.
One accent, Cut-Line Amber, kept for the primary action and the focus ring.
Charcoal near-black marks "you are here" and the strongest secondary actions.
Pill buttons, rounded cards and generous controls: friendly and sturdy.
Figures are always set in tabular numerals.
Light and dark themes come from one set of semantic tokens.

rules.name: The One Cut Rule
rules.body: Amber is spent on the single action that moves the job forward, and on focus. If two amber buttons sit side by side, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Status Means Something Rule
rules.body: Green, amber-warning, red and blue appear only to report a state: paid, overdue, failed, information. They are never decoration, and they always come with a word, because colour alone doesn't carry meaning.

rules.name: The Readable Ink Rule
rules.body: Every text colour, Ink Subtle and the status colours included, passes 4.5:1 on Surface, Board Cream and Surface Muted, in both themes. Amber is a fill and a focus ring, never text.

rules.name: The Token Only Rule
rules.body: Colour comes from the semantic tokens (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-muted`, `text-danger`), never from raw Tailwind palette classes (`text-amber-600`, `text-slate-500`) or hex. Raw values don't follow dark mode. Hundreds of them exist in the code today. That's drift to pay down, not precedent.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every quantity, price, margin, total and date in a column uses `tabular-nums`, so the digits line up. It's already used in nearly 300 places. A misaligned column of money is a bug.

rules.name: The Small Title Rule
rules.body: Inside the app, hierarchy comes from weight, position and ink tone, not from big type. Only the page headline goes above 0.875rem.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Controls are at least 2.5rem tall (inputs and default buttons). On screens used on the floor or on a phone, actions use the large button (2.75rem). The small button (2rem) is only for dense desktop toolbars and table rows.

rules.name: The Solid Sheet Rule
rules.body: Working surfaces are opaque. No frosted glass on cards, tables or dialogs. Blur is allowed only on the scrim behind a modal or drawer and on the sticky header.

rules.name: The One Dark Mode Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is the .dark class on the page, and Tailwind's dark: variant is bound to it in globals.css. Never let a style follow the operating system on its own.

dos: Do use the semantic colour tokens (`bg-surface`, `text-ink`, `text-ink-muted`, `border-border`, `bg-brand`, `text-danger`), so dark mode follows automatically.
Do keep one amber primary button per view, with On Amber text on it in both themes.
Do set every quantity, price, margin and date in `tabular-nums`, aligned to the right in tables.
Do use solid `bg-surface` for cards, tables and dialogs, with the Whisper shadow and a hairline border.
Do make primary controls at least 2.5rem tall, and use the 2.75rem button on phone and floor screens.
Do pair every status colour with a word, in a badge or an alert.
Do use logical spacing and alignment (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `text-start`/`text-end`) in new work, so layouts can flip for Arabic later.
donts: Don't drift towards a generic SaaS dashboard: no purple or blue gradients, no glassy frosted cards, no decorative charts without real numbers.
Don't drift towards a playful consumer app: no big illustrations, no emoji as interface, no bouncy or springy motion.
Don't use raw Tailwind palette classes (`text-amber-600`, `bg-slate-50`, `text-rose-600`) or hex values for interface colour.
Don't put white text on Cut-Line Amber.
Don't use type larger than 0.875rem inside cards. Only the page headline is large.
Don't let a wide table scroll the page. It scrolls inside its own card.
